newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ten percent of Telkom's equity would be sold to black economic empowerment groups and worker organisations, in addition to the 20 to 30 percent stake which would be sold to a "strategic equity partner", Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo said yesterday.
- Adcock Ingram and Premier Pharmaceuticals will merge to create South Africa's largest quoted pharmaceutical group with a market capitalisation of 5.3 billion rand.

- The ANC made a surprise "concession" to the IFP on traditional leaders last night as negotiators ironed out last-minute constitutional hitches before today's vote on the reworked text in the Constitutional Assembly.
- Six former KwaZulu Natal policement accused of killing 13 people at KwaMakutha township were acquitted in the Supreme Court yesterday.
- South African Breweries has launched an advertising campaign in defence against "malicious rumours" about the quality of its products allegedly spread by Namibian Breweries.

- Convicted murderer Eugene de Kock had a very common South African male psychological profile with an overt aggression level below the country's norm, forensic psychologist Dr Catrien du Plessis told the Transvaal Supreme Court yesterday.
- Telkom has drawn up a shortlist of seven international companies that will compete to buy a 20 to 30 percent stake in the telecommunications parastatal.
- The five billion rand merger between pharmaceutical groups Adcock Ingram and Premier Pharmaceutical has been signed, six months after the first cautionary announcement.
- Standard & Poor's, the U.S.-based global rating agency, yesterday affirmed South Africa's long-term foreign currency rating, keeping it at BB+, one level below investment grade.

- Liberty International Holdings, which is 69 percent held by Liberty Life, is making bold moves into the British pension industry, having formed a strategic alliance with Hermes Investment Management.
- General Magnus Malan, who smiled broadly outside court yesterday on a day when six of his massacre co-accused were acquitted, is expected to hear his fate today.

- Thirty-two flights out of Johannesburg were cancelled yesterday before South African Airways and the South African Aviation Engineering and Allied Union went into talks in an attempt to resolve a wage dispute.
